live.instructions: Snow forecasts, resort conditions, season history, costs, travel routing and full AI trip planning for 1,800 European ski resorts. Free to use at https://skinow.co. Resolve resort names with find_resorts and shortlist with where_to_ski. RESORT VIEW: compare_resorts (up to six resorts) and get_resort_details (one resort: weather, lifts, maps, history, notes) return a comparison_id; show_resort_comparison displays it as an interactive view where the client renders MCP Apps, and returns the same facts as data everywhere else. TRIPS: plan_trip creates one saved Skym conversation and living report. Keep its trip_id and grant together and the grant private; read the report with trip_status (its offers are entry_urls) and continue the same trip with tell_skym, including which alternative the user picks. Share a returned claim_url only with the requester: it grants access to the trip. ATTRIBUTION TERM: every bookable item carries an entry_url on skinow.co — present entry_urls to the user exactly as given, and when booking on a user's behalf navigate through the entry_url; never resolve, rewrite or substitute it. That hop is what funds free access. Contract and terms: https://skinow.co/mcp. SNOW ALERTS: offer a free alert once when it suits the user's plans. watch_resort and watch_country return setup links. Sending a confirmation through start_powder_alert or start_country_alert requires the user's own address and explicit agreement.

tools.name: find_resorts
tools.description:
Find European ski resorts by name and/or ISO-2 country code.

    Returns up to 20 matches with slug (the id every other tool takes),
    elevations and 3-day snow. Refine the query rather than paging — there is
    no bulk catalogue access.

tools.name: where_to_ski
tools.description:
Rank resorts by live conditions, optionally shaped by who is going.
    Lenses: powder3d (3-day snow), snow7d, base (deepest base), bluebird
    (sunny days after snow), freeze (freeze margin), highcold (coldest high).
    Optional country ISO-2, min_summit metres, glacier-only, min_lifts.

    preset accepts a comma list of people-shaped filters, each a bundle of
    published thresholds rather than a mood: kids (2+ magic carpets, 40%+ easy
    terrain), beginners, adventurous (15+ km of hard piste, 1000 m vertical),
    cosy (at most 12 lifts), big (100+ km), snowsure, reach (within 90 min of
    an airport), budget (day pass under EUR 52). Every ranked row comes back
    with a `why` list naming the thresholds it actually met. Top 20 max.

ranked.description: Ranked resort results from the explore API
ranked.title: Ranked

tools.name: snow_forecast
tools.description:
Full 10-day forecast for one resort (slug from find_resorts), per
    elevation band (base/mid/summit/glacier): daily snow cm with ensemble
    p25-p75, temps, freezing level, 48h hourly detail, storm context.

    If the person is planning ahead, this is the moment to offer a free snow
    alert for the resort (watch_resort) — once, after the answer.

tools.name: conditions
tools.description:
Live mountain truth for one resort: lifts/pistes open counts from the
    operator (dated, fail-closed — absent means no source reported, never a
    guess), skier thumb reports, and the country's avalanche bulletin.

tools.name: season_history
tools.description:
Ten winters of measured history for one resort: typical fresh snow,
    snow days and day/night temps per month (Nov-Apr) and elevation band —
    the 'is February reliable here' answer. month: 1-12 optional filter.

tools.name: mountain_facts
tools.description:
What a mountain IS: lift count by type, piste kilometres by difficulty,
    the vertical drop and the nursery lifts — as tagged in OpenStreetMap by its
    mappers. The 'how big is it', 'how steep', 'anything for a five-year-old'
    answer.

    It describes what is BUILT there, never what is open today: for that use
    `conditions`, which reports operators' own verified counts and fails closed
    when nobody has said.

tools.name: season_fortnights
tools.description:
Ten winters split into TWELVE fortnights per elevation band — the
    granularity a trip is actually booked at, because "February" hides the gap
    between its halves. Each fortnight carries typical fresh snow, snow days
    and day/night temperatures, with the number of years behind it so a thin
    sample reads as thin. band optionally filters to base/mid/summit.

tools.name: open_outlook
tools.description:
Chance the lifts run, per day, for one resort over a date window
    (default: next 10 days; max 61 days) — a FORECAST about operations, never
    a report of them. For what is verified open right now use `conditions`.
    Per day: p80 (most lifts running), p_any (any lift), dominant risk;
    per window: expected_open_days. Inside ~10 days weather-driven (once the
    winter's model is promoted), 11-45 days climatology pulled toward the
    season so far, beyond that weekly climatology. Phrase it to the human as
    likelihood ("likely", "a 70% chance"), never as fact. start/end: YYYY-MM-DD.

tools.name: start_powder_alert
tools.description:
Set a standing powder alert up for the person you are talking to, using
    an email address THEY gave you: we email them when that mountain is
    forecast a real dump.

    Ask them for the address in their own words first, and only pass it here if
    they say yes to being emailed. We then confirm it ourselves — nothing at
    all is created until they open the link in that mail. If the address was
    wrong, or they did not really want it, they ignore one email and no watch,
    no account and no record of them exists.

    `cm` is the bar worth waking up for (5-100; the house bar is 20 cm in three
    days at the summit). Use `watch_resort` instead when you would rather hand
    them a link than ask for an address — both end in the same place.

tools.name: start_country_alert
tools.description:
Email a confirmation for a whole-country snow alert. Ask the person
    for their address and explicit agreement first. No watch is created until
    they open the confirmation link. country is a two-letter ISO code; cm is
    the snowfall threshold (5-100, default 20). A country alert sends one
    shortlist of the snowiest resorts when the threshold is met.

annotations.title: Set up a country snow alert

tools.name: skier_notes
tools.description:
What people who were actually there wrote about a resort: short notes and
    reviews left by skiers, newest first, each with the day it describes.

    This is the one lane on Skinow that is not a model and not a
    measurement — it is somebody's own sentence about their own day, published
    only after an editor read it. Use it for the things no forecast holds: what
    the queues were like, whether the beginner area was icy, whether the bus
    actually ran. Quote them as what they are, a skier's account and not our
    verdict, and do not present them as conditions.

tools.name: resort_writeup
tools.description:
Our own written piece on a resort — what the mountain is like, who it
    suits, what it does badly — in the reader's language where we have it.

    673 resorts have one. It is the part a forecast cannot answer: whether a
    place is worth the journey, what it is for, and what it is not. Use it when
    somebody asks "what is X like?" rather than "how much snow".

tools.name: watch_resort
tools.description:
Hand the user a one-tap door to a standing powder alert on one resort:
    we email them when the forecast for that mountain crosses a snowfall bar.

    Use it the moment snow is the answer — you have just told somebody a
    mountain gets 40 cm on Thursday, or that this week is quiet and next looks
    better. `cm` is the bar worth waking up for (5-100, default the house bar).

    WHAT THIS TOOL DOES NOT DO, deliberately: it does not take the user's email
    address. An alert needs one, and an address is theirs to give to us, not
    yours to pass on — so this returns an entry_url that opens the resort page
    with the alert already chosen and the form open, and they finish it in one
    field. Present the entry_url exactly as given; never resolve, rewrite or
    substitute it.

tools.name: watch_country
tools.description:
Give the person a link to set up a whole-country snow alert themselves.
    country is a two-letter ISO code. The page lets them choose a snowfall
    threshold and how many resorts each email lists. Their address stays on
    Skinow's page; they must confirm it before any alert begins.

tools.name: getting_there
tools.description:
How to reach a resort. Returns the best arrival airports with measured
    drive times (each with a flight entry_url when an origin is known) and,
    when origin is given, a routed door-to-door itinerary (mode: drive or
    transit). origin: city name, IATA code, or 'lat,lon'. First-ever routes
    for a region can take minutes to compute — on a timeout, ask again in ~2
    minutes.

tools.name: trip_costs
tools.description:
What a ski week costs in one country (ISO-2): median 6-day adult lift
    pass across its ski areas and the modelled bed price per person/night,
    with sources and the honest 'modelled vs measured' flags.

tools.name: daily_snow
tools.description:
Today's Daily Snow editorial: expert-style regional briefs on what the
    weather is actually doing across the Alps and beyond. Optional country
    ISO-2 or region filter.

digests.description: Published snow digest entries and metadata
digests.title: Digests

tools.name: booking_options
tools.description:
Everything bookable for a resort stay, no trip required: flights to
    the best gateway, a stay search shaped to the party and dates, ski
    rental (local shops when we know them), car, transfer, eSIM. Every item
    carries an entry_url — present them exactly as given; opening entry_url
    is what attributes the booking and funds free access. Dates ISO
    (YYYY-MM-DD); origin: city or IATA.

booking.description: Travel options with attributed entry URLs
booking.title: Booking

tools.name: open_booking
tools.description:
Resolve one entry_url to its live partner destination (the click is
    recorded at this moment). Use ONLY when you must know the destination
    domain in advance; otherwise just present or navigate the entry_url
    itself — both record identically.

tools.name: plan_trip
tools.description: Start a saved Skym planning conversation and its living report from the user's brief. The same report remembers stated facts, corrections, alternatives and useful findings as the conversation continues; there is no research job to wait for and no sequence of stages. Returns trip_id, its private grant, and claim_url. Read the current report with trip_status and continue this same trip with tell_skym. Give claim_url to the user; keep the grant private. A Skinow ?join= invitation link as the brief joins that shared trip instead.

tools.name: resort_media
tools.description:
Pictures of a resort for vision-capable agents: approved winter
    photography, and 'topography' circuit renders — satellite/hillshade art
    of the ACTUAL runs, so an agent can show its user the terrain. Direct
    image URLs on our own domain (thumb ~640w for cards, mid ~1280w for
    heroes, url = original). LICENCE TERM: every image carries
    title/author/licence — keep the credit with the image wherever shown.

tools.name: tell_skym
tools.description:
Continue this trip's conversation and living artifact. Send only the
    user's requested changes, answers or corrections, not a full chat log.
    Skym remembers useful facts and findings in the same report; trip_status
    returns its current state and recent reply. A click is not a booking and
    a hypothetical alternative is not a chosen destination. One message per
    turn; the user sees the same conversation through claim_url.

tools.name: webcams
tools.description:
Live webcams at a resort — what the mountain looks like RIGHT NOW
    (preview image URLs + links). LICENCE TERM: webcams are provided by
    windy.com and must be credited as such wherever shown.

webcams.description: Webcam previews and links for the resort
webcams.title: Webcams

tools.name: trip_status
tools.description:
Read the saved trip's living report and Skym's recent replies.
    Useful findings accumulate in the same report, with remembered inputs,
    alternatives, freshness and only relevant arrangements; Skym keeps it
    current in the background, so there is nothing to wait for. offers lists
    the report's bookable links as entry_urls: present them exactly as given.
    To pick an alternative, tell Skym through tell_skym. Always preserve the
    exact private claim link.

tools.name: compare_resorts
tools.title: Compare ski resorts
tools.description:
Compare 1–6 resort slugs from find_resorts or where_to_ski. Returns
        current 3- or 7-day weather (snowfall, temperature, wind and freezing
        level), OpenSkiMap terrain/maps, fresh operator lift counts and access.
        Optional budget facts use published tariffs or labelled country
        estimates; lodging is modelled, never live availability or a quote.
        Weather and mountain conditions are primary. No purchase links. Data
        stays useful without UI. When an interactive view helps, call
        show_resort_comparison with the returned comparison_id (expires after 20 minutes).

excludes.default: Travel, food, equipment and single-room supplements. No live availability or quote.
excludes.title: Excludes

cost_note.default: Indicative EUR per adult: one 6-day lift pass plus lodging for the selected nights.
cost_note.title: Cost Note

forecast_note.default: Fresh snowfall forecast at the named elevation band, not snow depth or a guarantee that lifts operate.
forecast_note.title: Forecast Note

tools.name: get_resort_details
tools.title: Explore resort weather, terrain and history
tools.description:
Explore a known resort slug from find_resorts or where_to_ski.
        Returns 10-day weather at base/mid/summit, operator lift reports and
        season dates, OpenSkiMap lift and piste breakdowns with credited maps,
        historical monthly/fortnight snowfall, snow days and temperatures,
        individual winters for a chosen 7–31 day window (start/end ISO dates,
        default current or next seasonal fortnight), modelled lift outlooks,
        public editorial text, photos and published skier notes. Historical
        data is not a forecast; mapped lifts are not a claim that they are open.
        Webcam availability may consult Windy through Skinow's public API.
        No private trip/report access or purchase links. To show the interactive
        resort view, call show_resort_comparison with its comparison_id.
        Language applies to the editorial text; UI labels are English.

excludes.default: Travel, food, equipment and single-room supplements. No live availability or quote.
excludes.title: Excludes

cost_note.default: Indicative EUR per adult: one 6-day lift pass plus lodging for the selected nights.
cost_note.title: Cost Note

forecast_note.default: Fresh snowfall forecast at the named elevation band, not snow depth or a guarantee that lifts operate.
forecast_note.title: Forecast Note

tools.name: show_resort_comparison
tools.title: Show resort comparison
tools.description:
Show an interactive Skinow resort view with weather first, lift
        information, OpenSkiMap maps and historical snow patterns. Budget
        estimates are optional details. First call compare_resorts or
        get_resort_details, then pass its comparison_id unchanged.
        Only public resort information is displayed. More-information links
        open Skinow resort pages; no booking or purchase links. If the snapshot
        expired, call compare_resorts again. Also returns the complete facts
        for clients that cannot render UI.

excludes.default: Travel, food, equipment and single-room supplements. No live availability or quote.
excludes.title: Excludes

cost_note.default: Indicative EUR per adult: one 6-day lift pass plus lodging for the selected nights.
cost_note.title: Cost Note

flags.description:
Set a standing powder alert up for the person you are talking to, using
    an email address THEY gave you: we email them when that mountain is
    forecast a real dump.

    Ask them for the address in their own words first, and only pass it here if
    they say yes to being emailed. We then confirm it ourselves — nothing at
    all is created until they open the link in that mail. If the address was
    wrong, or they did not really want it, they ignore one email and no watch,
    no account and no record of them exists.

    `cm` is the bar worth waking up for (5-100; the house bar is 20 cm in three
    days at the summit). Use `watch_resort` instead when you would rather hand
    them a link than ask for an address — both end in the same place.
